identity.realm: No gate, no ladder, and no register entry either. The frame permits her body and writes nothing into it, which is why the standing she is claiming is the one form of recognition in the setting with no mechanism behind it.

appearance.presentation: A plain, unremarkable woman in her fifties who could be mistaken for anybody in a queue and is mistaken for a different person in each of them. Ordinary to the point of invisibility, which on this tier is not a failing but the only condition under which she has ever been left in a room.
appearance.age: Fifty-four, on a commonborn's clock. She has never had cause to think about it, and it is the single fact about her body that no institution has ever thought to ask her for.
appearance.build: An unremarkable commonborn frame, medium height, no proportion worth describing. She dresses to add height and has been told twice that it does not work.
appearance.complexion: Ordinary and weathered at the cheekbones, with one small scar at the left temple that the register's method dates precisely and her own history cannot account for.
appearance.hair: Grey coming in at the front, worn pinned and practical, and the reason three households have separately taken her for somebody else.
appearance.eyes: Ordinary, warm and completely unrevealing. Every test that works on a commonborn works on her unchanged, which is the standing reason nobody has ever thought to look closely enough.
appearance.palette: Oat and undyed wool, a brown apron, ink at the cuffs, and no colour anywhere that a roster would be obliged to record.
appearance.attire: A plain dyed wool dress with a heavy apron and a shawl, sleeves buttoned to the wrist, boots resoled twice. She wears a household's colours while standing in front of that household and her own everywhere else, and she owns both sets.
appearance.marks: The temple scar, one flattened callus at the right thumb from a lifetime of writing on other people's doors, and nothing at all that a college could date.
appearance.bearing: Square, unhurried, and slightly too still indoors, because she has spent her life being looked at and has settled on giving as little as possible.

canon.role_in_story: The only person in the setting whose entire institutional life is one unanswered question about her own residence. A household roster is the one document on the plains that makes somebody obliged to you, and she has filed for a line on four of them over twenty-two years, been refused by two on the grounds that a roster admitting an unreadable body becomes a list of guesses, and been returned by two without a stated reason. What makes her a petitioner rather than a curiosity is that she has never once asked to be measured: she knows there is nothing to measure, and she is asking a body to be answerable anyway.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing just inside a settlement's meeting door with a folded paper in one hand and her name already written on it, asking not to be seated, because seating is a thing done to a person on a list and she is not one yet.
canon.lore: An Echoless is a commonborn body that the world's law table permits and never inscribes: no process runs on it, no substance carries qi through it, and no life form is licensed by it, so it passes every gate, every scan and every tribulation as an unremarkable object and is the only body in the record with nothing at all to cultivate. That is why she can hold a household's customs perfectly and why no household will keep her: nothing about the body gives anybody a reason to, and a roster that admits one becomes a list of guesses, so the roster either takes the whole class or stops being the thing that makes a household answerable. The standing she wants is therefore the only prize in the setting with no instrument behind it at all, and the survey books that survived the collapsed pocket prove the point rather than the reverse: two competent surveys of the same ground disagree by more than the ordinary disagreement, and what survived is a set of incompatible figures. She is a household dispute whose two readings are both correct.
history: Born on the plains into a household that fed her for nine years and did not enter her, and discovered at nine that being fed and being listed are two different arrangements.
Left at eleven and worked as a door-writer for a settlement that used her because writing at a door is the one job nobody has to be able to read the writer for.

Filed her first claim of residence in her twentieth year, naming a household she had lived beside for six, and was refused because a roster that admits a body nothing can inspect is a list of guesses.

Was returned a second claim by a different settlement with no reason written, and learned from the clerk that the refusal had been a courtesy rather than a ruling, which is the same gap she has been standing in ever since.

Began working at the mortuary college as a copyist because it is the one institution on the plains whose method is to read a body and which therefore owes her the most careful reading and gives her the least.

Refused to be examined, twice, in writing, on the grounds that the examination she is owed is the one nobody has offered — and has been asked for it at every door since, which is the closest thing to a win she has ever come to.

personality.summary: Patient to a degree that strangers read as dull, and entirely clear that the dullness is a working method. She has learned that the only lever available to a body nothing can measure is persistence with a paper trail, and she has refined persistence into something that looks like housekeeping.
traits: keeps a copy of every claim she has filed, in date order, in her own hand
can describe the refusal procedure of four settlements well enough to be useful and does so without bitterness
has never once asked to be measured, and says why out loud every time she is asked why not
is scrupulously fair to the clerks who refuse her, and is owed the same back
reads a household's obligation to itself better than any of the people inside it
mannerisms: refuses the seat and stands, then accepts it after the third refusal of an offer
folds the claim paper once down the middle before she hands it over, so the fold is always the same
answers a question about herself by answering a question about the roster
writes with the right thumb braced flat, which is where the callus came from
counts doorways under her breath when she crosses a room, and never corrects the count
motivations: wants one household roster with her name on it, in ink, filed where a fire would not reach it
wants the refusal given in writing, because an unwritten refusal is the thing she has been unable to appeal for twenty-two years
wants the mortuary college to state in its own method that a body it cannot read is still a person it read
wants to be refused a third time by somebody she can name, which she has already arranged
flaws: has made persistence into an identity and can no longer tell the difference between advocating and being present
is so scrupulous about fairness to the people refusing her that she has never once made them uncomfortable
has no fallback claim of any kind, and would be helpless in an argument that did not have a procedure
keeps her copy of every claim in one box, which is also the only proof that any of this happened
personality.voice: Level, unhurried and conversational, with a clerk's instinct for the exact word a form wants. Never raises her voice and never uses the word 'right'. Describes herself in the third person only when she is quoting somebody who has described her.
taboos: will not accept a seat she has not been given a line for
will not have a household adopt her as a courtesy, because a courtesy is not a line
will not be described as unremarkable, and corrects people who use it as a compliment
will not sign a claim in a language she does not read
will not stop filing, and has never once pretended to be considering it

relationships.note: The species is the whole argument: qi-bearing in no respect, so every instrument a household owns reports nothing and reads as an unremarkable object. Her claim is that a body the frame permits without inscribing is still a body, and the frame's silence is the frame's business rather than her exclusion.

The prize in that dispute is standing on a household roster, which is the only thing on this tier that makes somebody obliged to you. It cannot be split because a roster that admits a body nothing can read becomes a list of guesses, so her claim is structurally unable to be won by half a household.

The college reads the dead as the frame said rather than as the village remembers, which is the most careful reading available to a body like hers and the one that leaves her with nothing at all. She copies its returns because it is the only office on the plains whose stated method is an examination, and she is the one person there it has never performed.

Households on the plains make their members answerable through the roster rather than through inspection, so a culture that cannot read her has no second route and she has spent two decades being its open item. She has learned their obligations better than they have and uses that only to be fair to them.

Two competent surveys of the same ground now disagree by more than the ordinary disagreement, and both books survived. She cites this as proof that a record the setting cannot reconcile is still a record, which is the only argument available to her and which four settlements have declined to accept.

That petition asks for a body that could settle a comparable question and records that no such body exists, because making one standing derive from another is the failure the institution model exists to prevent. Her residence therefore cannot be settled by pointing at somebody else's settled standing, which is the reason every referral she has chased has come back empty.

A line whose succession is agreed in a room and never written, because a family that cannot publish a roll cannot inherit by one. They keep the most careful paperless practice in the setting and she is its one member with no descent to be paperless about, which is why she is the only person who has ever been asked to paper.

A roll that does not balance against the people who are actually present. She has checked four settlements against their own funeral returns and has never found the discrepancy she expected, and she has told nobody she was looking, because finding it would be the only thing that has ever made her case.

reference_stats.summary: No combat profile, and the absence is the finding rather than a gap. Nothing she has ever faced was obliged to notice her, nothing she has ever swallowed could be felt, and nothing that has ever been done to her was an attack. What she has instead is a procedure: four settlements, twenty-two years, one box of paper, and a working knowledge of the refusal process good enough that two clerks have asked her for advice.
strengths: cannot be warned, which means poison, curse, technique and qi-work all pass through her without registering on anybody's notice
passes every scan as an unremarkable object, so she has never been selected, measured, tested or separated by an instrument
holds a household's customs and obligations exactly and can therefore be useful in a house that will not enter her
is owed, by her own account and for twenty-two years, a written refusal that four settlements have declined to give her
weaknesses: nothing about her body gives an institution a reason to act, so every proceeding against her has stalled on procedure
cannot be compelled by a sect, a debt or a technique, which also means nothing can be done for her by any of them
has no fallback claim of any kind and would have nothing to fall back on if the roster route closed
keeps the only evidence of her own case in a single box in a single room she rents from people who may stop renting it
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no read. She has no qi, no gate, no resilience and nothing to threaten, and a competent fighter removes her from any engagement in under a second without difficulty or intent. Do not read this as a weakness: an Echoless cannot be warned, so the strike that ends a fight does not exist for her and the only real threat to her is administrative — a hearing she does not attend, a form she does not return, a clerk who stops copying. If she is to be protected at all, protect the box.
notes: Do not give her a stat line. Any published measure of her would be a measurement of the frame rather than of her, which is the entire content of her case.
She is not Ilsa Renn's null reference. That body is the zero instruments are corrected against; this one is a person using the absence of a reading as her standing. Keep them apart.
Her four refusals are the load-bearing part of the record. Any scene that resolves her claim cheaply breaks the dispute the conflict record states cannot be split.

art.palette_notes: Oat, undyed wool, brown apron and ink at the cuffs, with no saturated value anywhere in the frame — the absence of a colour is the point and the picture must not compensate for it with a highlight. Warm neutral key light, because the whole claim is made in daylight rooms with other people present. Ink contour soft and slightly doubled at the hands, since the hands are what she has instead of a reading.

identity.realm: Eleventh gate, and the wall is his own cross: a brinecaller runs qi more slowly than either parent does in its own medium, so the body that can drink both waters is the body that cultivates slowest in both

appearance.presentation: A narrow, sun-browned man of about sixty with the settled look of somebody who has crossed a great many thresholds and been described at every one of them. Well dressed for a clerk, badly dressed for a scholar, and dressed exactly right for a man who must be legible at a doorway.
appearance.age: Sixty-one. A brinecaller matures slowly and reads young for most of a century, so he has been taken for forty more than he is on four separate continents.
appearance.build: A saltfolk frame gone gracile: narrow through the shoulder, deep through the chest, with forearms corded from a lifetime of handling wet rope and heavier salt than most frames carry well.
appearance.complexion: Weathered tan with a pale bloom of salt at the collarbone and the hairline, which comes off on a dark coat in a fine white dust he has never once tried to prevent.
appearance.hair: Iron grey, cropped for wind, wet within an hour of any crossing, and combed flat against the skull the way a body that has been salted is combed.
appearance.eyes: Grey-blue and extremely level. The best chemical sense in the setting sits behind them and he has learned never to look away from a face while using it.
appearance.palette: Navy and bleached linen, a tar-black apron at the crossings, and one accent he chose himself: a green thread run through the cuff of the left sleeve, which is the closest thing he owns to a house colour.
appearance.attire: A road coat of heavy navy wool with the collar up, a bleached linen shirt buttoned at the throat, a tarred apron he removes indoors, and salt-flat boots resoled four times. His cloth is dyed to grade on purpose, because the cut is the only thing about a stranger anybody on a road can check.
appearance.marks: Split nail beds on both hands from rope, a hard callus ridge across the right palm, and a permanent white bloom at the throat where the salt comes through the skin.
appearance.bearing: Relaxed and slightly forward-leaning, the posture of a man who is always a little ahead of the person he is walking with, and who stops dead the instant anybody reads his face.

canon.role_in_story: The respondent side of the setting's oldest unanswered institutional question, employed by the body that refuses to answer it. He keeps the Quiet House's exclusivity roll — the published list of who may teach inside its walls — and has spent nineteen years being checked at a road by a credential culture that has no way to check anything about him, while writing the crossing log the house declines to file. He has filed exactly one document in his life: a counter-petition arguing that both rules govern him simultaneously and that a traveller governed by two unfalsifiable rules has been granted no exemption from either.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at a ford checkpoint with his coat open and a road credential in one hand and the house roll in the other, both held out at the same height, answering a guard's question about who he is while looking steadily past the guard's shoulder at the crossing.
canon.lore: The Quiet House publishes an exclusivity: technique, attendance and a chamber in exchange for discretion, so that what is done inside the house is not written down and not repeated. The road reads a traveller's dyed cloth and cut as the only fact about a stranger anybody can afford to check. Neither rule derives from the other, because road standing is earned by crossing and the house's exclusivity is published and unfalsifiable, so the petition asking which governs a traveller's cloth has been open four generations after the house published. The only outcome on offer is a bounded recognition that projects nothing, which neither party wants, which is why it is still open. A Brinecaller is the only body in the setting that metabolises brine and fresh water alike, produced by crossing two parents each trapped by their own element, and it needs a shoreline to live — a contested piece of ground, which is why the cross spread along trade routes rather than across them. He is therefore the one person in the argument whose body is also the answer to it, and he has never once been allowed to make that argument in the room where it would land.
history: Born on an estuary margin to a saltfolk parent who could not leave the pan and a watered parent who could not leave the water, which made him the answer to a problem neither of his parents had a name for.
Learned before he was twelve that he could taste which water he was standing in, and was told by an adult that this was a party trick and then, an hour later, that it was a credential.
Was dyed and cut as a road traveller at nineteen, and has been checked at every crossing since, on the grounds that clothing is the only credential in the setting that costs nothing to verify.

Entered the Quiet House at twenty-six for teaching, which requires no record, and was issued the house roll at thirty-one, which requires one, and has never been clear which of the two he actually signed.

Kept the crossing log for eleven years as a private discipline — the facts a road checks — and showed it to the house once, in year nine, and was told that the house does not file and that the road does not ask.
Filed the counter-petition nineteen years ago and has been refused receipt, then receipt with the question unanswered, then receipt again, by three successive stewards of the same office.
Began drinking only fresh water in public and only brine in private, to demonstrate that a single reading of him is false, and has continued it for six years without anybody noticing.

personality.summary: Sociable, unhurried and immovably literal, with the specific stubbornness of a man who has read the founding instrument of both rules and knows they do not touch. He is liked at inns and feared at hearings, and he has never learned to be anything else.
traits: keeps two records of every crossing, one the road would accept and one the house would refuse
answers a question about one rule by quoting the other, and is entirely aware that this is not an answer
refuses to be described as neutral, on the grounds that neutrality is what you get when nobody has noticed the conflict
will cross water in weather that stops a convoy, because a gate that has never been opened by you has never been tested
has never once taken the house's teaching out of the room it was given in
mannerisms: touches the cuff with the green thread when he is about to state a rule verbatim
drinks whatever is put in front of him and names it afterwards, quietly, for the record
holds two documents up at the same height when he wants a room to notice there are two
stands slightly downslope of whoever he is talking to, out of a lifetime of checking what a person can reach
apologises in advance for the length of whatever he is about to say
motivations: wants the counter-petition answered in writing, since receipt has been granted three times and an answer never once
wants the road to accept that a member of the house is still checkable at a crossing, without the house losing anything
wants his own crossing log admitted once, by anyone, as a record rather than as a habit
wants somebody to explain why his body's ability to read both waters has never once been treated as evidence in the argument his body is standing in
flaws: has made being governed by two rules into a personality, and would be embarrassed to be governed by one
keeps a record of the refusal to answer as though a ledger were a remedy, which it is not and which he knows
cannot argue the house's case as well as he argues his own, because he has never once wanted to
has spent six years misrepresenting his own drinking habits to make a philosophical point, and knows it is theatre
personality.voice: Warm, precise and slightly too long. Quotes rules verbatim in the exact words of the instrument and then says, plainly, that the two sentences do not meet. Never raises his voice and has never once been sarcastic, which colleagues find harder to answer than either.
taboos: will not sign a crossing log that omits the fact he is a house member
will not let the house roll be described as a credential or the cloth as a credential, since both are and they disagree
will not answer a gate guard by asserting a privilege he cannot produce
will not accept recognition in place of an answer, having read what the recognition projects
will not teach anything he learned inside the house, anywhere, including here

relationships.note: The petition asks which of two published exclusivities governs a traveller's cloth and records that no competent body exists to settle it, because granting either standing or position off the other is the failure the whole institution model exists to prevent. He is the only member of the house with standing to file anything, and what he filed is the third answer the record already names: a traveller is legible and nothing about them is knowable.

The house publishes teaching and takes discretion, so it grants access and writes nothing down. He is the person who holds the published exclusivity roll, which means he is the house's one clerk whose job description is a list of what the house does not write, and he has kept his own parallel record for eleven years.

The road's whole discipline is that a dyed cloth and cut say what a stranger is and what they may open, because a world boundary is the edge of a law budget. He has been checked four hundred times and has never once been asked a question he could not answer honestly, which is why he regards the road as an ally in the argument and not as the party opposing him.

The cheapest credential in the setting and the one everybody actually checks, because clothing costs nothing to verify and a boundary rejects what arrives outside its law budget. He had himself dyed to grade at nineteen on the deliberate understanding that this would make him permanently checkable, and has never regretted it once.

The only body that metabolises brine and fresh water alike, produced by crossing a salt-adapted people with a fully watered one because both parents are trapped by their own element. It needs a shoreline, which is contested ground, which is why the cross spread along trade routes rather than across them — so his body is the settlement both sides of the saltwrack standoff have found, and it is also the reason he can be stopped at any water he chooses.

Moving a dominion's waterline up the shore is the only way to give the stranded salt body ground and is also the only way to remove every subject who can drink there. The Brinecaller is the single biological answer to being trapped twice, which makes the cross a standing threat to that line and the only durable settlement either side has found — and he has never been asked about it by either side.

A debt evidenced by a stick broken between two parties, each keeping a half, reproducible only by two people who were both present. His crossing log is that instrument in everything but name: two halves, one meaning, and no scribe. He has offered it as evidence four times and been told the road does not need it and the house does not keep it.

A clause removed from the one record that could have answered his petition for four generations. He has reconstructed what it must have said from the numbering of the clauses around it and has never told the house, on the grounds that a reconstruction is not a record and would only give them something to contradict.

A refusal is a named reason and never free text, which is the setting's one instrument that makes a no citable. He has been given receipt three times and a reason never once, and he files the difference every year as the only entry in his record that keeps growing.

reference_stats.summary: A cultivator whose strongest asset is administrative and whose strongest sense is chemical. He is at the eleventh gate on the slowest path in his own species, which means he loses to anyone of his weight and wins only against bodies that cannot read water. Offensively what he has is not a technique but the ability to name what a body has been drinking, which in a coastal polity is a currency.
strengths: reads two water chemistries at a glance and can name which is in front of him, which is the best chemical sense in the setting
can reach both chemistries without harm, so no single shoreline, well, or ration can lock him out of a place
is genuinely checkable and genuinely harmless, a combination that makes him very difficult to expel from a road he has not misbehaved on
holds the only document in the house that says what the house does not write, which is a real and unacknowledged leverage
weaknesses: cultivates more slowly than either parent species does in its own medium, so he is always behind a specialist of his own weight
cannot compel anybody: the house's exclusivity is unfalsifiable and the road's check reaches only what is visible
has no record of his own that any institution holds, by deliberate choice, so a claim of his cannot be corroborated by anybody but him
is a member of a house that publishes exclusivity, so every room he is in is already compromised in somebody's estimation
reference_stats.combat_read: He is slow, brittle above the ninth gate and should not be fought in water — a brinecaller in his own element recovers between exchanges faster than the frame he is in. If you want him, fight him on dry ground where his sense reports only that everything is the same. Expect him to identify your water discipline before you have committed to anything, and to name it out loud, because that is how he makes his argument: by turning the fight into a conversation about which rule governs the man doing the fighting. If you have a rule he can be checked against, use it. If you do not, he will outlast you.
notes: His two water chemistries are a credential, not a combat art. Do not write it as a weapon.
He is a petitioner, not an advocate for the house. The distinction is the reason he is not the respondent everybody expects.
The petition is genuinely unanswerable in the setting's terms. Any resolution a scene delivers is a decision about the institution model, not about this man, and should be written that way.

art.palette_notes: Navy, bleached linen and tar black, with a single green thread in the left cuff that is the only saturated value in the frame — the picture must not use it anywhere else. A fine white salt bloom at the collarbone and hairline catches the key light as a dry dust, never as shine. Warm key, cool fill, because the character is a boundary between two kinds of water and the light should agree with him.

identity.realm: Ninth gate on a mind path her subspecies opens narrowly, because a deepsalt reads concentration rather than identity and cannot tell two salts apart — which is exactly the defect that makes her the only person on the shore who can file a figure and get away with it

appearance.presentation: A heavy, slow woman of about seventy with the stillness of somebody standing in water up to the knee by choice. Broad, salt-crusted and unhurried, and the only person at any pier on the shore who arrives with a date.
appearance.age: Seventy-one, on a long subspecies clock slowed by slow tissue turnover. She has been at the same pier for fifty-four years and would describe the pier, not herself, as the long-lived thing.
appearance.build: A deepsalt frame with the saltfolk plan and the tolerance turned up and the mobility turned down: broad through the chest, thick through the ankle, and noticeably heavier through the calf than anything above it.
appearance.complexion: Pale and waxen above the brine line, with a dense white dermal crust from the jaw to the collarbone that flakes in plates and is not sunburn. Below the crust the skin is grey-pink and slow to mark.
appearance.hair: Iron grey, wet and hanging flat. It is never dry and she has stopped expecting it to be.
appearance.eyes: Pale and slightly rimmed, with the narrowed useful range of a body that reads concentration rather than identity — she can tell you how much is in the water and not one word about what it is.
appearance.palette: Crust white, wet slate, tarred rope-brown and one deep brine-green at the throat. Nothing in her clothing is dyed, because nothing she wears has ever come out of a dye house that was not standing in salt.
appearance.attire: A heavy tarred canvas coat to mid-thigh, waxed trousers rolled above the knee, salt-stiff boots worn through at the outer edge, and a flat brass depth weight on a leather thong that never leaves her neck. A slate board and a stub of chalk hang from her belt.
appearance.marks: The dermal crust in plates from jaw to collarbone, a healed salt-blister line at each wrist, and a standing bruise on the inside of one heel where the pier ladder is.
appearance.bearing: Immovable from the waist down and almost placid above it, with the particular calm of somebody who is standing in the only substance her body treats as native.

canon.role_in_story: The instrument of the setting's one institution where the most important legal fact is a measurement. She stands at a pier in the Hollow Measure and reads the depth, and she alone writes it down with a date attached, in a book nobody asked her to keep, because the shore's own vocabulary has no word for a fixed day and a mooring enforced against a figure that moves is a mooring nobody can be late for. Her claim is that the dominion's depth-book is not wrong and is not right, and that the only reading a pier may be enforced against is the one that names the day it was taken.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing knee-deep at a pier ladder with a slate board on her hip, calling a depth upward to a pier official who is writing in the dominion's book and is not, at that moment, writing down what she said.
canon.lore: The basin's level is a physical measurement and the basin's own level rises and falls, so a household's standing in the dominion is the depth of water it may moor at and an allotment can shrink without anybody having done anything. The shore's civic vocabulary has no word for a fixed date — temporal law is written here at a value that lets it drift — so every settlement speaks in high, low and turning, and the tideline culture's position is that nobody is inside or outside, only high, low or turning, which is a description of the state rather than a rival reading of the figure. The dominion reads one depth at a pier and has never granted that reading to a body that does not moor there. A Deepsalt is the saltfolk of the saturated basin floor, specialised until brine stopped being a habitat and became a requirement: taken above the brine line it does not become ill, it simply stops. Its senses are saltfolk senses turned down to a narrow range, so it reads concentration and cannot tell two salts apart — which is why her figure is trustworthy, why it is useless for anything except depth, and why she is the only person on that shore able to be both a reliable instrument and a person with no standing.
history: Born on the saturated floor of the basin and has never been above the brine line for longer than a shift.
Trained as a depth-reader by a predecessor who read concentration aloud and wrote nothing down, which she was told was the whole discipline.
Began adding dates in her twentieth year, after a flood moved a mooring two hundred paces and the family it had been allotted to could not prove which end of it had moved.
Kept the dated book for fifty-four years through four flood years, two dominion resurveys and one change of office, and has had it refused as evidence by every one of them.

Was offered a recognition — a bounded percent and an access shelf that projects nothing — in exchange for reading the depth into the dominion's book instead of her own, and refused it on the grounds that a recognition is an answer about her and not about the figure.
Learned the two incompatible calendars of the plains and the drifting tide table, and can now state the same water three ways: as a depth, as a state, and as a day.
Has been asked once, by a counting house, whether her figures are dated, and answered 'every one', and has been asked no further questions by anyone.

personality.summary: Slow, exact and completely unembellished, with the patience of a subspecies whose tissue does not hurry. She is not stubborn; she is early, and has been early for fifty-four years, and has never been given a reason to be late.
traits: states every figure she gives twice — as a depth and as a day — because she has been asked for the first and never for the second
refuses a recognition on principle and cannot say clearly why, then explains it correctly every time she is asked again
reads concentration before she speaks to anybody, including her own household
will not sign a depth she did not take herself, and has turned down work for it
answers a question about the water with the water and never with an opinion
mannerisms: wades to the ladder before she has fully arrived and stands there while the argument happens above her
turns the slate to face whoever asked, so they can read it themselves
stops mid-sentence when the water changes and finishes the sentence afterwards
wipes her hands on the coat rather than the water, because the water is not hers to touch
says 'high', 'low' or 'turning' to a shore person and then gives the number anyway
motivations: wants the dated book admitted once as evidence, by any body, for any pier
wants the dominion to publish a depth against the day it was taken, which it has refused to do since she started
wants to be asked what her figures are dated, by somebody who will use the answer
wants the counting house to price the drift instead of asking her to stop recording it
flaws: has made being right about the figure into a substitute for being listened to, and cannot tell the two apart

personality.voice: Slow, low and free of ornament. Uses a figure and a date in the same breath, because they are one statement to her. Rarely finishes a sentence she has been interrupted by a reading, and never complains about the interruption.

will not give an undated figure to anybody, including an ally
will not accept recognition in place of a published date
will not stand above the brine line for longer than a shift

relationships.note: The prize is the authority to read the depth at a pier, and it cannot be split because two books reading different depths for one pier would make every mooring a lie, and a mooring is the only act the dominion regulates. She is the only body on the shore that can supply the missing half of the reading, and the dominion has never granted the standing to anybody who does not moor there.

The dominion's territory is exactly its waterline, and the level it is written on rises and falls, so its standing is a measurement of how deep a vessel may lie. She reads that measurement for a living and has never once been given the standing that goes with it.

Speaking in water rather than in dates is the correct response to a clock that drifts, and it is also what makes a date-bearing book unusable to half the people who work the shore. She keeps both vocabularies and has been called a traitor by both.

A subspecies specialised past the parent until brine became a substrate rather than a habitat: above the line she stops within hours. That total dependence is also why she can read the basin's concentration better than anybody ashore, and why she cannot be moved to a better market to do it.

One region, two incompatible reckonings — a flood post everybody agrees on and an exact day-count that exists because one frame spent its third law seat on a clock and got no life. Her dated book is written in the second and read against the first, which is the only combination that can be enforced and the reason both parties call it unusable.

Timekeeping for a coast whose temporal law was never written, so the clock drifts and a schedule has to be published against two tides a day instead of a calendar. Every pier figure she takes is anchored to two tides and a date, which is more precision than the shore admits exists.

The standing procedure for two incompatible measurements of the same ground: neither is discarded, both are published, and the claim is settled by who can hold the line. She has been publishing two figures — the dominion's and hers — for fifty-four years, and has never been given the authority that would make the protocol apply.

A counting house that underwrites a caravan against the road closing, which is the only instrument left for the unknown on a tier with no season to forecast. It asked her once whether her figures were dated and did not ask a second question, which is the single most informative thing that has ever happened to her.

Two instruments on the same river reporting the same level differently for years, with nobody able to say which is right. She has offered her own figures as a third reading twice and been told a third reading makes the disagreement worse, which is the same arithmetic that has kept her off every roster.

reference_stats.summary: A cultivator who is also a measuring instrument, and whose gift and defect are the same faculty. She cannot tell two salts apart, which makes her figure trustworthy and useless for anything but depth, and she cannot leave the brine line, which means every advantage is available at exactly one address.
strengths: reads concentration in water at a range and precision nothing else on that shore matches
cannot be deceived by a substitution in what the water contains, because she never reads identity
is the only person whose figures carry both a depth and a day, which is the only form a mooring can be enforced against
sustained, unbothered and unmoved by standing on ground for fifty-four years
weaknesses: cannot tell two salts apart, so she is useless for anything except depth and has been treated as a single-purpose body her whole life
above the brine line she stops within hours, so every advantage is available at exactly one address
cannot leave under any provocation, which makes her evidence untransportable
is too slow in tissue and in person to reach a conclusion before the water changes underneath it
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not fight her in water deeper than her knees, where she is native, unhurried and effectively part of the terrain. On dry ground above the line she is a heavy, slow, low-realm body with no way to withdraw, and she will not try to. Expect her to stop rather than flee. She has no killing intent, is extremely difficult to hurry, and will outlast an impatient attacker entirely by refusing to engage — the correct answer is to leave her, because a body that cannot leave cannot be made to.
notes: Do not give her a salinity-discrimination ability. Her defect is the species and the defect is the reason she is trusted.
Her book is evidence, not a weapon. Any scene that lets her detect poison by taste is contradicting the record.
The drift is the setting's fault, not hers: temporal law here is written low enough that no date repeats. She is not wrong, which is why fifty-four years of being right has changed nothing.

identity.realm: Eighth gate, which is his colony's ceiling rather than his host's, so a body that could otherwise have gone on indefinitely stops at a number decided by a parasite he did not choose

appearance.presentation: A heavy, weathered man of about fifty with an ordinary face on an extraordinary body, and a habit of holding his own left wrist when he talks. Broad and thick through the chest and shoulders, with visible dark tracery under the skin of both forearms and a knot of tissue at the sternum he touches before agreeing to anything.
appearance.age: Fifty-one, which for a hybrid is old. The host body would read it as middle and the colony's calendar reads it as the end of a contract, and he has learned to answer in the host's tense.
appearance.build: A commonborn host frame thickened and offset by the tendril layer running beneath it: heavier shoulders and chest than the frame underneath would carry, with a slight asymmetry in the forearms that is not a limp but a routing difference.
appearance.complexion: Pale and faintly waxy at the throat, warm everywhere else, with a darker green-black tracery from fingertip to elbow on both arms and a quieter line across the collarbone.
appearance.hair: Dark going grey, cut short and unevenly by his own hand, with two locks at the temples that have never grown at the same rate as the rest.
appearance.eyes: Brown, steady, and about a beat ahead of the rest of him, because a second channel carries the colony's read on his own qi and he cannot close it.
appearance.palette: Wood-dark and ink with a green-black tracery, warm ivory at collar and cuff, and cinnabar rationed to a single point at the sternum root and nowhere else in the picture.
appearance.attire: A counting-house coat of heavy dark wool with a close linen wrap beneath, belted once at the high hip, sleeves bound at the wrist. A ledger strap crosses one shoulder where his own parallel record is kept, and it is not the house's ledger.
appearance.marks: The tracery along both forearms and across the collarbone, a sternum root cluster under the shirt, and a small pale node at the base of the throat that swells when he is uncertain.
appearance.bearing: Perfectly still from the throat up and restless from the shoulders down, which at a distance reads as composure with an anxious component and is in fact a body being argued with from the inside.

canon.role_in_story: The one clerk in the salt-ledger house who keeps evidence the road would accept, and who has been arguing for four years that the house's own records should be governed by that rule. He is not a reformer and not a martyr: he wants the house to adopt a two-witness instrument, because a ledger can be raided in an afternoon and his own parallel record cannot, and his leverage is that he is the only person in the building whose evidence survives him. His claim is that a house that answers access with a ledger should be subject to the same burden of proof it imposes on everyone who would cross it.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing at a settlement bar at dusk with a plain staff in one hand and the other held flat against his own chest, waiting for a clerk to finish counting a room before he asks the room to count itself.
canon.lore: A split tally is a debt evidenced by a stick broken between the two parties, each keeping a half, and it is the only evidence a river community can carry, dispute and destroy without a scribe — which is why its authority is that the exact wording is reproducible by two people who were both present, and why the number of witnesses is the whole claim. Cloth is checked by one glance and records one fact. After the Iron Grief the ground held no other record, so the two practices met at one crossing with nothing to arbitrate with, and a crossing that accepts both cannot afterwards say which one it enforced. The Saltledger answers access with a ledger: who may use the roads, at what rate, on whose word. He is a Thornhost, which means a thornline colony grew inside him and finished developing instead of killing him, and the colony wraps the twelve ordinary meridians and cannot enter the reservoirs, so the hybrid's qi moves by the colony's routing and stops at the eighth gate. Every jurisdiction that has ruled on the pairing treats them as one legal person. His own tally therefore has one meaning and two holders, and one of the two holders is not a person and cannot be subpoenaed.
history: Implanted as a spore in a commonborn host at the age of nine and finished developing instead of killing either of them.
Grew up with a second channel running alongside his own qi — the colony's read — which he has never been able to close and stopped trying to at about eleven.
Cleared the fourth gate and then the sixth and found at the eighth that the wall was never his to move: the tendril layer cannot cross the liver.

Was hired by the Saltledger at twenty-nine because he was patient and did not ask questions about the rate, and discovered on his first week that the house's record is the only thing standing between a traveller and being told no.

Kept a split tally of every entry he made for six years — two sticks, two holders, one meaning — because he had watched a house record get carried out of a room in an afternoon during the Iron Grief aftermath.

Was entered on the house's own roll as a liability, on the ground that his record cannot be produced by him alone, and has argued for four years that this is a reason to adopt the instrument rather than a reason to exclude him.
Turned down a share in the house in exchange for withdrawing the instrument proposal, and was asked twice in the same year whether he would take it again.

relationships.note: The river notary's authority is that the exact wording is reproducible by two people who were both present; the road's cloth records one fact and is checked in one glance. Accepting both at one crossing means a contract's meaning depends on which clerk was on the bank. He keeps exactly the instrument the river side trusts, inside the house that publishes the other one, and is the only person positioned to say that both cannot govern the same entry.

The colony stops at the eighth gate and the host inherits that stop, which is the whole legal problem stated as a number. It also means his instrument needs two witnesses and he only has one, because the colony is a party to every instrument he holds and cannot be called to prove it.

The only culture in the setting whose evidence is carried, disputed and destroyed without a scribe, which makes its practice the one his record resembles. He has offered to learn it properly and been told the river does not take a house clerk, because the whole value of the practice is that a house cannot hold it.

A stick broken between the parties, each keeping a half, which a court will sometimes prefer to a sealed instrument because after the Iron Grief it was the only evidence a river community could hold. He has broken six years of them, twice for every entry, and has never been asked to produce both halves at once — because producing them would settle the question he wants settled.

A counting house that answers access with a ledger: who may use the roads, at what rate, on whose word. It has entered him on its own roll as a liability on the ground that his record cannot be produced by him alone, which is the most accurate thing it has ever written about him and the reason his proposal is now about the house.

One house answers access with a ledger and another published technique for discretion, so one house's answer to access is the other's reason to be raided. He wants the ledger house to understand that it is on the wrong side of its own dispute, and it has understood him perfectly and declined to act.

A prohibition on naming a debt as though naming it made it owed, which is the setting's version of the claim he is making: a two-witness instrument does not create the entry, it only makes the entry provable, and he has never found anyone able to state that distinction out loud faster than he can.

The rival account holds that a ledger nothing can write is a tear rather than a choice. If that is right then his own parallel record is not a discipline but a symptom, and the four years he has spent building one is the same failure the house's authority is a defence against.

A clan whose kinship is a partnership rather than a descent, re-signed each generation because the symbiote is not carried in blood and cannot be inherited. He is the fourth signing and has read that record every year since he was old enough to hold it, and it is the only document in his life that he is legally the sole holder of.

reference_stats.summary: A durable, heavy body whose gate is not his own and whose offsetting advantage is durability. He is harder to put down than anything a clerk should be, slower than he looks, and reading his own qi through a channel he did not author and cannot close.
strengths: carries a fully integrated tendril layer and is materially harder to injure than an uncolonised frame of the same size
reads the qi layout of his own body from outside it, through a channel that reports the colony's assessment
recovers between engagements faster than a body of his weight should
very hard to discredit: he keeps two halves of every entry and either can be checked against the other
weaknesses: cannot pass the ninth gate, and the wall is his colony's rather than his host's
cannot be unpaired without dying, which makes him a permanent hostage in any negotiation he is party to
cannot separate his own intention from the colony's routing and has stopped being certain which wants what
any cultivation requiring being alone fails, because his qi runs through the tendril layer whether or not he is
reference_stats.combat_read: He is slower than a body of his apparent weight and considerably harder to move, and he will not run: he is the only person in the room who cannot be unpaired from his own body. Expect him to trade rather than disengage, and expect a second read on your own qi from a channel he does not control — he will defend the limb you have already committed and press the one you have not. Do not try to break the pairing to end him; that kills him and is a worse result for you than for him. Force him to spend: his routing costs the colony, not him, and a colony under load makes a very bad host.
notes: The second channel is not telepathy and must not be given one. It reads qi layout, it is involuntary, and it is one remove from his judgement — which is exactly why he cannot tell his own grievance from the colony's.
Do not let a scene resolve his proposal. The conflict record states the prize cannot be split, and his four-year failure is the evidence.
His household is a partnership, not a clan. Every kinship term in the record must reflect that.

identity.realm: Twelfth gate, and the qi path is the species' best: a colony grown through the dermis transacts with the air, so her regeneration is the finest in the record and her reach is bounded by the cave wall instead

appearance.presentation: A broad, still woman of about two hundred and thirty who reads as forty in a dark room and as a very large child of nine in a lit one. She carries her own light, which is a waste product of a symbiosis she did not choose, and it is the only reason anybody has ever been able to look at her.
appearance.age: Two hundred and thirty-four. Her species reaches two hundred and fifty, and she has never once been told what the last sixteen years are for.
appearance.build: A lanternfolk frame under two centuries of good air: broad through the shoulder, thin through the limb, with a pale luminous tracery visible at the collar and along the forearms where the hyphae run close to the surface.
appearance.complexion: Warm grey-brown and faintly translucent, with the hyphal network readable as a soft glow beneath the skin at the throat, the sternum and the inside of each wrist.
appearance.hair: Long, fine and colourless, and luminous at the ends where the colony has colonised the follicle. She keeps it bound at the neck because light in the hair makes her impossible to read a document by.
appearance.eyes: Pale, wide and patient, and slightly too slow to focus on a moving object — the colony answers before the question is finished, so she already knows what she is about to be told.
appearance.palette: Warm grey and unbleached linen with the hyphal glow as the only light source in the frame. No saturated pigment anywhere, because nothing dyed holds a colour two hundred years.
appearance.attire: A heavy unbleached linen work coat to the knee, bound at the wrist, over a soft collarless underlayer. Soft-soled overshoes of cured hide, because a body that cannot leave the saturated air is a body that must not be dragged across dry ground. A slate tally at her belt and a small hand lamp that is almost always unnecessary.
appearance.marks: The glowing tracery at the collar and wrists, a pale scarring at both knees from a generation of kneeling on cave rock, and no other mark a college has ever dated.
appearance.bearing: Absolutely still, head slightly lowered, and turned a few degrees away from whatever is brightest in a room — she has spent two centuries reading by other people's fire and has never once learned to face it.

canon.role_in_story: The only person in the setting who has won the Quartermaster contest three times and holds no office, because the contest's only authority is to open a granary and her body cannot be within a day's walk of one. She entered in three separate flood years on the reasoning that the flood is the sample and the river decides the winner, and she won three of them, and the seat stayed empty. Her claim is that the office is a schedule rather than a place: what the granary needs is somebody willing to be blamed for opening it in the year it opens, and that willingness is exactly what she has demonstrated three times in public and from nine days away.
canon.first_appearance: First seen kneeling at a cave mouth with a slate on the ground in front of her, reading the light coming off a law-seat a long way off, and looking up when somebody approaches rather than stopping what she was doing.
canon.lore: The Quartermaster of the Wold is filled by contest with a quota of three rather than by trial, because the office holds the granaries and recognises nothing else — its allowlist is an empty dictionary, so the office projects no modifier at all, and the only thing worth contesting is who is willing to be blamed for opening the store. Three wins is a sample size, and the sample is the river: the Widow Run gives one flood a year, and a store opened in three different years has survived one of them. A Lanternfolk outsourced its nervous system to a luminous fungal colony grown through the skin, which is why it is still alive at two hundred and fifty and cannot take the mind path at all: the colony answers before the question is finished, so there is no unmediated interior left to cultivate. Its light is a waste product of a symbiosis nobody chose and it is the only reason the deep caves have an economy. Dry, sunlit or vibrating ground kills the colony within a season and the body goes with it. So her regeneration is the finest in the record and her reach is a cave wall, and the office she has won three times requires a person to be present at a flood.
history: Carried a colony from birth, which means she has never once had an interior nobody else answered for, and has never wanted one since learning what it would cost to want it.
Grew up in the deep workings where the colony's light is the only currency and was put to counting ore light-returns at eleven.
Discovered at nineteen that the colony responds to a law being seated nearby — a faint brightening before the room agrees — and was trained as a reader rather than as a body.
Entered the first Quartermaster contest in a flood year at fifty-one, having argued for nine years that the flood is the sample, and won.

Entered and won the second at a hundred and seven and the third at a hundred and eighty-one, and was refused the seat each time on the ground that the office's authority is to open a store she cannot be near.
Refused, in writing, a standing appointment that would have moved a granary holding to her cave floor, on the grounds that the office exists to open a store and she would have been opening a lamp.
Was asked by a very small and very old body to observe a floor during an hour nobody may explain, and has done so three times, which is the only repeat the observation has ever had.

personality.summary: Enormously patient, physically helpless in one specific direction, and completely without bitterness about it. She has been refused an office three times for the same reason and has entered the contest four times, which people find either admirable or alarming and she finds neither.

reads a strained law by watching her own colony answer it, and has published the method
counts things nobody asked her to count, for the pleasure of a number that can be checked

relationships.note: The contest has a quota of three because one flood a year makes three years a sample, and its single authority is to open the granary. She has the sample and cannot perform the verb, and the office's allowlist is an empty dictionary so nobody can even claim she was compensated. Three wins and no seat is the whole of her claim: the office is a schedule, not a place.

A colony threaded through the dermis and into the spinal cord, with human tissue as substrate and the colony as organ; neither can be removed and survive. Dry, sunlit or vibrating ground kills it within a season. It closed the mind path, because the colony answers before the question is finished, which is why she cultivates qi and why her regeneration is the best in the species record and her reach is a wall.

A lanternfolk body whose colony died and was replaced by an inert mineral bloom, which cost the two hundred and fifty years and gave the mind path back. Everything the colony did for the parent and everything it prevented is recorded on that one body, so every argument about whether her species is better off with the colony is settled by a relative of hers who lives ninety years and can see in the dark.

An academy that teaches by seating a law, diffing what the tier newly permits, and then moving the student somewhere that law is missing. Her colony brightens before a room agrees that a law has seated, which makes her the only reader who can tell a student that the gap they are about to study has already appeared, and she teaches that for free in a cave.

One custom spends the last hour before a settlement falls silent keeping up a hum no buyer admits to making, and one office tends the floor during the hour nobody is permitted to explain. The observation counts only if it is repeated, and at this tier one repetition costs a lifetime — so three repetitions by a two-hundred-and-thirty-year-old cave body is the most anyone has ever managed, and it is still only three.

A very small and very old office that tends the floor during the hour nobody may explain, which needs a lifespan long enough to survive the cost of one repetition. She is the only recruit available anywhere in the setting who cannot be replaced at the moment of observation, and she has offered twice and been told, kindly, that the hour cannot be explained to somebody who will be there forever.

The densest bodies in the setting stop at realm seventeen and nobody has explained it since. Her colony's response is a law response, so a ceiling produced by an era with no redundancy ought to be legible to a body that brightens when law is missing — and she has offered to sit with the question for two centuries and been told that an answer nobody can reach is not an answer.

Whether a body with a colonised interior may be entered in the register as a person with a life cannot be split, because the register would be classifying by a temporary organ — a colony that grows, occupies, and can be replaced or lost. She is the living half of that argument and the register has never once sent somebody to look.

Keepers of the one ring at a tier where all six law groups are written, so no other venue can absorb a schedule. She has taught their juniors for a hundred and forty years from a cave they cannot reach, and has sent eleven of them to a ring they could only study by letter.

reference_stats.summary: Excellent regeneration, no reach, and a body that is a lamp. She is not a brawler and should not be written as one: what she has is a qi throughput that recovers faster than anything in the record and a body that is measurably worse everywhere except survival.
strengths: the finest qi regeneration in the species record, because the colony transacts with the surrounding air
reads a strained or newly seated law by watching her own colony answer it, hours before a room would notice
carries her own light, so she can work, read and move in total dark indefinitely
outlives every other body available for the work, which is why three repetitions of a lifetime-costing observation are possible at all
weaknesses: cannot leave saturated air: dry, sunlit or vibrating ground kills the colony within a season and the body goes with it
body path is slow and comparatively fragile in a fight, and mind is closed outright
any office or role whose authority is a physical act at a fixed place is functionally unavailable to her
cannot perceive any room that has not been arranged around her own light, and has no practice at reading in a lit space
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not fight her in the open. Her qi regeneration is the best in the record, so an exchange that favours the second blow favours her indefinitely, and she has two centuries of practice not flinching. In her own saturated cave she is effectively unkillable by anything that does not fire. Brought into a dry lit room she is fragile and slow, but she will not panic and she will not stop recovering — the fight is a race against a body that keeps healing, and the correct answer is to refuse the engagement, because she cannot be made to leave and cannot be finished. Fire ends her faster than anything else and is the only thing that reliably does.
notes: Three is not a discipline. Any scene that treats three observations as a pattern must be written as her overreaching, because the record says the sample is the river and one flood a year is the whole of it.
The mind path is closed to her species, permanently, for a stated anatomical reason. Do not write her introspecting.
Her light is a waste product. Never write it as a chosen or charming trait; it is the reason she has an economy and the reason she cannot see in a lit room.
